votes.evidence: /tmp/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:126-138 queues a review because TaskRun output supplies a PR target, not because GitHub emits ready_for_review. The separate webhook carve-out rejects ready_for_review at stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:160-168; its stated reason is that the transition alone does not invalidate an existing draft-time verdict. tests/test_tasks.py:835-854 names this behavior ready_for_review_keeps_the_draft_verdict. review_pr.py:587-590 likewise states that an approval granted on a draft is meant to take effect when it becomes ready. The receiver's worker only rejects closed PRs at tasks.py:1166-1169 and intentionally supports later same-URL/new-head recovery at 1125-1128.
votes.refutation: I first traced the source of the review and the exact ready-state contract. In the proposed ordering the TaskRun output already triggered the review while the PR was draft; executing that accepted task after the flag flips is not a new review triggered by ready_for_review. No code or test says the transition cancels queued/in-flight reviews or withdraws their eligibility. The contract instead preserves approvals across that transition and permits subsequent synchronize/reopen/base-retarget reviews. Requiring draft=true in the worker would discard a legitimate delayed initial review and constrain the recovery path, without fixing any demonstrated correctness/security defect. The finding conflates trigger selection with review eligibility.

votes.evidence: The actual ready_for_review policy is event-specific: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:160-167 says that flip alone does not invalidate an existing draft-time verdict and therefore does not trigger another webhook review. Its test expressly names that behavior 'ready_for_review_keeps_the_draft_verdict' (tests/test_tasks.py:835-844). The initial review has already been requested by the opted-in TaskRun output event; tasks.py:1113-1128 describes its current-head/recovery semantics, and 1166-1174 permits any still-open current head. The engine's own comment says the draft approval should take effect on the ready PR (tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:587-590). votes.refutation: I checked whether 'ready does not trigger a new review' meant 'an otherwise authorized review must never run while ready.' The source distinguishes those situations: the webhook event is intentionally a no-op while approvals remain valid across that transition, and later synchronize/reopen/base-retarget deliveries can still review the same identified PR without any draft-state requirement (tasks.py:160-176). The delayed initial review examines the current head, whose identity is rechecked before posting at temporal/activities.py:673-685. Requiring draft=true would discard requested reviews solely because triage happened before queue execution. The claimed behavior violation is a contradicted premise.
